topic.title: JavaScript Essentials
topic.description: The language of the web. Variables, functions, async, DOM — the must-knows.

items.prompt: Which keyword creates a variable whose value CAN be reassigned later?
What happens if you reassign a const variable?
options: A TypeError is thrown at runtime

items.prompt: What is the scope of a variable declared with 'let' inside a {} block?
options: Block-scoped — only accessible inside that block

items.prompt: What does this code log? `const arr = [1, 2]; arr.push(3); console.log(arr);`
Which declaration is HOISTED but throws ReferenceError if accessed before its declaration line?
Which is NOT a primitive type in JavaScript?
What does `typeof null` return?
Which value is FALSY in JavaScript?
What's the difference between `null` and `undefined`?
options: null is an intentional 'no value'; undefined means a value was never assigned
null is a number, undefined is an object
null is for objects, undefined is for arrays

items.prompt: What is the result of `0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3`?
What's the difference between `==` and `===`?
options: === checks value AND type without coercion; == coerces types before comparing

items.prompt: What does the `??` operator do?
options: Nullish coalescing — returns the right side only if the left side is null or undefined

items.prompt: What does `user?.address?.city` do?
options: Asks the user if they want to access city
Throws an error if user is undefined
Safely accesses nested properties, returning undefined if any link is null/undefined

items.prompt: What does the spread operator `...` do in `[...arr1, ...arr2]`?
options: Expands arr1 and arr2 into individual elements of a new array

items.prompt: What does `2 ** 3` evaluate to?
Which is an arrow function?
options: function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
const add = function(a, b) { return a + b; }

items.prompt: What does this return? `function greet(name = 'World') { return 'Hello ' + name; }; greet();`
What is a 'callback function'?
options: A function that returns to a previous page
A function passed as an argument to another function, to be invoked later

items.prompt: What is a 'pure function'?
options: A function that always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects
A function written in pure JavaScript
A function declared with the 'pure' keyword

items.prompt: What does `arr.map(x => x * 2)` return?
options: A NEW array with each element doubled

items.prompt: What is a 'closure' in JavaScript?
options: A way to close a browser tab
A keyword to end a function
A function that 'remembers' variables from the scope where it was defined, even after that scope exits

items.prompt: What does this counter pattern demonstrate? `function makeCounter() { let n = 0; return () => ++n; }`
options: A pure function with no state
A closure capturing private state n

items.prompt: What is 'lexical scope'?
options: Scope is determined by where code is written, not where it's called from
Scope only applies to global variables
Scope is determined by who calls the function

items.prompt: What does the `this` keyword refer to inside a regular function called as `obj.method()`?
options: The object before the dot — obj

items.prompt: Why don't arrow functions have their own `this`?
options: They inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical scope, which avoids common bugs in callbacks
They have a hidden this that's hard to access

items.prompt: Which method REMOVES the last element from an array and returns it?
What does `[1,2,3,4].filter(x => x > 2)` return?
What does `[1,2,3].reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0)` return?
Which method finds the FIRST element matching a condition?
What does the spread operator return when combining arrays? `const c = [...a, ...b];`
options: A new array containing all elements of a followed by all elements of b
An array of two arrays: [a, b]
The shorter of the two arrays

items.prompt: What does this code log? `const o = {a: 1}; const p = o; p.a = 2; console.log(o.a);`
Which is the CORRECT way to make a shallow copy of an object?
What does destructuring do? `const {name, age} = user;`
options: Extracts named properties from user into individual variables

items.prompt: What is shorthand property syntax? `const obj = { name };`
options: Equivalent to { name: name } — uses the variable name as both key and value

items.prompt: How do you iterate over an object's KEYS?
What is a Promise in JavaScript?
options: A guarantee from JavaScript to run code
An object representing the eventual result (success or failure) of an asynchronous operation

items.prompt: What are the three states of a Promise?
What does .then() return?
How do you handle errors in a Promise chain?
options: Add .catch() at the end of the chain

items.prompt: What does `Promise.all([p1, p2, p3])` do?
options: Returns a Promise that fulfills when ALL inputs fulfill, or rejects on the FIRST rejection
Runs the promises one at a time

items.prompt: What does the `async` keyword do to a function?
options: Makes it return a Promise automatically, and allows `await` inside it

items.prompt: What does `await` do?
options: Pauses the async function until a Promise settles, then resumes with the resolved value

items.prompt: How do you handle errors with async/await?
options: Promise errors don't work with await
Wrap the await in a try/catch block

items.prompt: What's the MISTAKE in: `async function fetchAll() { const a = await fetch(u1); const b = await fetch(u2); return [a, b]; }`?
options: The fetches run sequentially instead of in parallel — use Promise.all

items.prompt: Can you use `await` at the top level of a module?
options: Yes, in ES modules — top-level await is supported

items.prompt: What is the DOM?
options: A tree-like programming interface representing the structure of an HTML document

items.prompt: Which method selects the FIRST element matching a CSS selector?
How do you change an element's text content?
How do you attach a click handler to a button?
What is 'event bubbling'?
options: When an event fires on a child, it propagates up through parent elements
When events appear in a popup bubble
When events bubble away into nothing

items.prompt: What does `fetch(url)` return?
options: A string of the response body
A Promise that resolves to a Response object

items.prompt: Does fetch reject on HTTP error status (404, 500)?
options: No — it only rejects on network failures. You must check response.ok manually

items.prompt: How do you send a POST request with JSON body using fetch?
What is CORS?
options: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — a browser security model controlling cross-domain HTTP requests

items.prompt: How do you parse a JSON response from fetch?
What does template literal syntax look like?
What does the rest parameter `...args` do in a function signature?
options: Collects all remaining arguments into a real array

items.prompt: What is a JavaScript module?
options: A file that uses import/export to share code with other files

items.prompt: What's the difference between default and named exports?
options: Default: one per module, imported by any name. Named: many per module, imported by exact name

items.prompt: What does `class Foo extends Bar {}` enable?
options: Foo inherits properties and methods from Bar (prototype-based inheritance with class syntax)

items.prompt: How do you catch a synchronous error in JavaScript?
What's the BEST way to handle an error that you can't recover from?
options: Log it and let it propagate with `throw` — don't swallow it silently

items.prompt: What is `throw new Error('message')` doing?
options: Creating a new Error object and throwing it as an exception
Logging an error to the console

items.prompt: What's a custom error class useful for?
options: Distinguishing different error types so catch blocks can react differently (ValidationError, NotFoundError, etc.)
Making errors look prettier in the console
There's no reason to use them

items.prompt: What is an 'unhandled promise rejection'?
options: A rejected Promise with no .catch handler — modern Node and browsers will warn or crash on these

items.prompt: What does `Boolean('false')` return?
What does `'5' + 3` evaluate to?
What does `'5' - 3` evaluate to?
What does `[] == false` evaluate to?
options: true (== coerces both to numbers, both become 0)

items.prompt: What's a SAFE way to check if a variable is null or undefined?
options: if (value == null)  — intentionally uses == to match both null and undefined

items.prompt: What does `localStorage.setItem('key', 'value')` do?
options: Persists a key/value string in the browser, surviving page reloads

items.prompt: What's the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
options: localStorage persists until cleared; sessionStorage is wiped when the tab closes

items.prompt: What does `setTimeout(fn, 1000)` do?
options: Schedules fn to run AFTER at least 1000ms (non-blocking)
Adds 1000ms to the page load time

items.prompt: What is the Console API mostly used for?
What does `window.location.href = 'https://example.com'` do?
options: Navigates the browser to that URL
Fetches the page in the background

items.prompt: What does `JSON.stringify(obj)` do?
options: Parses a JSON string into an object
Converts a JavaScript object/array to a JSON string

items.prompt: What does `JSON.parse(str)` do?
options: Converts a JSON string into a JavaScript value

items.prompt: Why might `JSON.stringify({a: undefined, b: 1})` surprise you?
options: The undefined value is omitted from the output: '{"b":1}'

items.prompt: What's the safe way to deep-clone a JSON-safe object?
Can a JSON file contain comments?
options: No — pure JSON does not support comments

items.prompt: Which loop iterates over the VALUES of an array?
Why is `for...in` BAD for iterating arrays?
options: It iterates keys as strings and includes inherited properties — order is also not guaranteed
It only works in old browsers

items.prompt: What does `.forEach` NOT support that a for loop does?
options: break and continue — forEach can't be exited early

items.prompt: What does `Array.from({length: 5}, (_, i) => i)` produce?
How do you iterate over an object's [key, value] PAIRS?
options: for (const k in obj) — only gets keys

items.prompt: Which keyword should you AVOID in modern JavaScript?
What does 'use strict' do at the top of a file?
options: Enables stricter parsing and error handling (e.g., assigning to undeclared variables throws)

items.prompt: Why is mutating function arguments BAD?
options: It causes surprising side effects for the caller and breaks the principle of pure functions
It is forbidden in strict mode

items.prompt: What is the 'principle of least surprise' in JS?
options: Code should behave the way readers would intuitively expect — favor clarity over cleverness
Hide as much logic as possible

items.prompt: Which is a HEALTHY rule of thumb for modern JS?
options: Prefer const, use === over ==, prefer immutability, handle Promise rejections, type your data (TS)

items.prompt: What is npm?
options: Node Package Manager — installs and manages JavaScript libraries

items.prompt: What's the purpose of `package.json`?
options: Lists a project's dependencies, scripts, metadata, and other config

items.prompt: What is a 'bundler' like Vite or Webpack?
options: A tool that combines, transforms, and optimizes your source files for production

items.prompt: What is TypeScript?
options: A superset of JavaScript that adds static types, compiled to JavaScript before running

items.prompt: What does ESLint do?
options: Statically analyzes JS/TS code to flag stylistic and potential bug issues

items.prompt: What's the FIRST thing to do in a new JS project?
options: Run `npm init` (or scaffold via Vite/CRA/Next), commit to git, write a README
Start coding immediately with no setup

items.prompt: Why are AUTOMATED TESTS valuable in JS projects?
options: They replace the need for understanding the code
They are only for big companies
They catch regressions when you change code, enable safe refactoring, and document expected behavior

items.prompt: What's the value of a `.gitignore` file in a JS project?
options: Excludes node_modules, build artifacts, secrets, and .env files from version control

items.prompt: When debugging in the browser, which tool is MOST powerful?
options: DevTools' debugger with breakpoints, watch expressions, and the call stack

items.prompt: What's the best way to keep IMPROVING at JavaScript?
options: Build real projects, read good code, write tests, learn the standard library deeply, follow MDN
